_note: A HANDOFF, NOT A REGISTRATION. Session C2 (lane AZ) walked these four routes end to end on
2026-08-31 and hands them to the lane that owns lib/control-plane/campaign-finance/obligations.ts
and the scheduler. NOTHING HERE WIRES ANYTHING: this file is read by a person or by that lane,
and no scheduler reads it. Two lanes writing one canonical store is what the integration rule
refuses, so the registration is theirs to make.
THE FIELD NAMES MATCH lib/workstate/types.ts ON PURPOSE - Disposition, PermissionState and
TransportState are that file's closed sets, so a registration can be written from these rows
READ THE routeUniverseWarning BEFORE REGISTERING THE FIRST ROUTE. It is the one thing here
that contradicts a completeness claim already recorded elsewhere in this repository.

filingAuthority.name: Arizona Secretary of State
filingAuthority.statutoryQuote: The secretary of state is the filing officer for statewide and legislative elections
filingAuthority.scope: Statewide and legislative offices only. Arizona is a FEDERATED filing state: 109 filing jurisdictions (1 State, 15 County, 93 City/Town) per Jurisdictions.txt. County and municipal candidates file elsewhere and these routes do NOT answer for them.

routeUniverseWarning.claim: A publisher-declared recordsTotal is complete FOR THE QUERY THAT WAS SENT, and is not the source universe.
routeUniverseWarning.whyItMatters: ShowOfficeHolder=true REPLACES the set rather than widening it - it returns 16 rows, disjoint from the default 370. A candidate behind either flag, asked for with the defaults, returns nothing, and recording that as 'no reports on file' is an absence manufactured by our own query.
routeUniverseWarning.concreteCost: Kevin Volk, candidate for Arizona State Representative District 17 on the 85701 and 85641 pilot ballot with $173,742.29 raised and 45 of 45 published committees reconciled, is NOT among the default 370. Matching the pilot ballot against the default view alone writes a false absence on his card.
routeUniverseWarning.action: Register the UNION of the three filter settings as the route's acquisition, not the default view.

routes.label: SeeTheMoney candidate/committee summary, union of all three filter settings
routes.method: POST (server-side DataTables: filters in the query string, the columns[N][data] array in the form body)
routes.recordClassNotYielded: Itemised transactions. This route yields per-office, per-party CYCLE TOTALS only.
routes.permissionEvidence: robots.txt HTTP 404 on 2026-08-31, identically to a bare client, an identified client and a browser-identified client - so the 404 is about the host, not about our identification. No terms document (/PublicResources/TermsOfUse HTTP 404). No challenge, no credential, no authentication of any kind. Re-confirmed from the 2026-08-24 and 2026-08-29 readings.
routes.executorNeeds: No browser, no session, no credential. The body must include the columns[N][data] array or the endpoint answers HTTP 200 with a two-byte empty string.
routes.cadence: The state's own filing calendar. Next Standing Reports deadline after 2026-08-31 is Post-Primary Election (Q3), 2026-10-15, read from ftp://ftp.azsos.gov/cfsdata2/ReportingPeriods.txt.

routes.label: SeeTheMoney itemised transaction ledger, per committee
routes.method: POST, Page=20 income / 21 expense / 24 all, and entityId=<committeeId> IN THE QUERY STRING
routes.permissionEvidence: Same host and same reading as the summary route.
routes.executorNeeds: The entityId parameter is LOAD-BEARING AND ITS ABSENCE IS SILENT: with Name=1~<id> alone the endpoint answers HTTP 200 with a complete, well-formed DataTables envelope and recordsTotal 0. That is a failed extraction wearing an absence's clothes, and an earlier session recorded this route as yielding nothing because of it.
routes.privacyConstraint: EVERY ROW CARRIES CONTRIBUTOR NAME, OCCUPATION, EMPLOYER, CITY AND ZIP (RULING 167). This lane reads them to compute a per-committee SUM and persists aggregates only. A scheduler registration that stores the rows would be a new personal-data class and is an ask-before, not an implementation detail.
routes.whyItIsRegistered: It is the only INDEPENDENT statement of a committee's cycle total, and it is what licenses every figure in data/states/az/funding/state-money-az-2026.json. Registering the summary route without this one re-creates the exact position that blocked Arizona for two sessions.

routes.label: Arizona committee register and filing calendar, anonymous FTP bulk drop

filesRetrieved.Committees.txt: 8,829 committees with type, organization date and termination date
filesRetrieved.ReportingPeriods.txt: 506 reporting periods with Cycle, ReportName and FilingPeriodEndDate

routes.permissionEvidence: Anonymous FTP, no credential, and the Secretary of State's own Bulk Filing Guide publishes the path. https://apps.azsos.gov/robots.txt answers HTTP 200 on 2026-08-31 with Crawl-delay: 5 and disallows /apps/, /scripts/, /poll/, /election/EOC2015/ and /cptest/ - no rule reaches the FTP service. NOTE: https://ftp.azsos.gov/robots.txt is a CONNECT TIMEOUT because there is no HTTPS service on that host; that is TRANSPORT state and is not a permission verdict (RULING 182).
routes.executorNeeds: A raw TCP FTP client. No FTP dependency is installed in this repository; scripts/state-money-az.mts carries a minimal PASV/RETR implementation the scheduler can lift.
routes.whatItDoesNotCarry: NO TRANSACTIONS. The Bulk Filing Guide is an UPLOAD specification for committees filing INTO the system; there is no documented bulk download of the money itself. Confirmed again on 2026-08-31 by listing the directory: 14 files, none of them transactional.
routes.whyItIsRegistered: It is the SECOND REPRESENTATION an absence has to clear. The portal being quiet about a person is not the register being quiet about them, and only both together are evidence about the record (RULING 206). It also supplies the next_due date every OURS_GAP renders.

routes.label: Arizona election results bulk drop, 1998 through 2026
routes.permissionEvidence: Same host, same anonymous access, same reading as the register route.
routes.note: NOT WALKED BEYOND THE LISTING, and it is out of this lane's scope - it is results, not money. Recorded because the FTP root was previously documented as if /cfsdata2/ were the whole of it. The root holds FOUR directories: cfsdata, cfsdata2, ElectionResults and 'EzBulkFilling Deploy'. ElectionResults carries a directory per even year from 1998 to 2026 inclusive, with the 2026 directory modified 5 July. Nothing in this repository has walked it.

obligationStillOpen.statement: Four Arizona pilot candidacies end in an OURS GAP and their obligation is LIVE, not closed.

candidacies.name: Tom Horne
candidacies.whatIsOwed: The register holds 100587 'Thomas Horne for Superintendent of Public Instruction', live and unterminated, with $918,092 of 2025-2026 income. Our name test cannot bridge the diminutive Tom/Thomas and must not guess one. Owed: an authoritative statement that the ballot's 'Tom Horne' and the filing's 'Thomas Chalres Horne' are one person - the candidate filing itself is the obvious source.

candidacies.name: Walter "Les" Presmyk
candidacies.whatIsOwed: Committee 102016 'Presmyk for Mine Inspector' matches on name and cycle, and the agency states NO office for it in the structured OfficeName field. Owed: the office as the agency states it somewhere structured. Inferring it from the committee's own name would be reading a marketing string as a filing.

candidacies.name: Genoveva Diaz
candidacies.whatIsOwed: Committee 102071 'DIAZ FOR AZ' matches on name and cycle with an empty OfficeName. Same shape as Presmyk.

candidacies.name: Sally Ann Gonzales
candidacies.whatIsOwed: Several committees match on name; one states State Senate District 20 and another State Senate District 3, neither of which is the House seat on this ballot, and a third states no office. She is a sitting senator running for the House, so publishing the Senate committee's money under the House candidacy would be a wrong figure under a real photograph. Owed: her 2026 House committee, or a sourced statement that the Senate committee IS the vehicle for this candidacy.

obligationStillOpen.readerVisible: Yes. Each of the four renders an OURS_GAP on its ballot card naming what we could not settle and the 2026-10-15 deadline. RULING 224's promotion tail is attached; the obligation is visible rather than silent.
